name: Chip supply
value: TSMC halts some China orders at 16nm and below
summary: New US rules from 19 Nov led TSMC and Samsung to pause some chip work for Chinese customers pending licences
state: New US Commerce Department rules effective 19 Nov removed a route that let some Chinese chip designers obtain advanced manufacturing without individual licences; TSMC has halted affected orders at 16nm and below unless customers obtain US licences (Reuters via The Standard, 19 Nov; Taipei Times, 20 Nov). The FT reported that TSMC and Samsung suspended some shipments to Chinese customers. New controls keep Watch; TSMC and Samsung output itself was not reported disrupted as of 27 Nov.
for_you: Chinese chip designers and the device makers that use their chips are most exposed; supply elsewhere is not reported affected, though controls can lengthen lead times for some components.
rubric_hit: Watch: new US export controls effective 19 Nov; no major disruption to TSMC or Samsung output

sources.title: The Standard (Reuters) — TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole
Taipei Times — report on TSMC orders under new US rules

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
